claim: Benavoli, Corani, and Mangili's mean-ranks critique was published in the Journal of Machine Learning Research, volume 17, in 2016, not 2015.
scope_conditions: Publication header of the JMLR version
quoted_support: "Journal of Machine Learning Research 17 (2016) 1-10" ... "Submitted 11/14; Revised 3/15; Published 3/16"

claim: The mean-ranks post-hoc test's outcome for a comparison between two specific algorithms A and B depends on which other algorithms are included in the same experimental pool, unlike Wilcoxon-signed-rank-based pairwise comparisons.
stance_target: N9's citation of Benavoli for 'mean-rank conclusions depend on the pool of compared methods'
scope_conditions: Statistical comparison of multiple classifiers over multiple datasets, general methodological result with worked examples
quoted_support: "the outcome of the mean-ranks test depends on the pool of algorithms originally included in the experiment. In other words, the outcome of the comparison between algorithms A and B depends also on the performance of the other algorithms in the pool."

claim: Benavoli et al. show concretely that for any pool of algorithms, the Wilcoxon-signed-rank-based decision about a specific pairwise comparison stays fixed, while the mean-ranks-test decision for the identical pair changes depending on which other algorithms are in the pool.
stance_target: the pool-dependence mechanism underlying N9's citation of Benavoli
scope_conditions: Worked numerical example with algorithms C1-C5 and additional algorithms C, D, E
quoted_support: "for any pool of algorithms C2, C4, Cx, Cy, we always report the same decision: C2, C4 are [significantly different]" [via Wilcoxon] versus the mean-ranks conclusion which "clearly depends on the pool of alternative classifiers"

claim: Benavoli et al. recommend replacing the mean-ranks post-hoc test with the sign test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test for statistical comparisons in machine learning, medicine, and psychology.
scope_conditions: General recommendation across scientific fields using multiple-algorithm comparisons
quoted_support: "the aim of this technical note is to discuss the inconsistencies of the mean-ranks post-hoc test with the goal of discouraging its use in machine learning as well as in medicine, psychology, etc."
